questions.q: What is the real advantage a BI-heavy capstone like this one has when it comes to live demos?
options: The dashboard itself is both the most impressive thing to show and the fastest, most legible thing to demo live
BI-heavy projects never need to describe anything from a diagram
Power BI dashboards cannot fail during a live demo
There is no real advantage compared to an infrastructure-heavy project
questions.explain: Unlike infrastructure components, the finished dashboard is immediately legible to any interviewer and is the actual deliverable the business asked for.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend describing the Airflow DAG graph and dbt lineage graph from a diagram rather than live?
options: They're dense and easy to misread quickly on a shared screen -- a verbal walkthrough against a diagram is clearer than live scrolling
Airflow and dbt cannot be demoed live under any circumstances
Interviewers are never interested in orchestration or lineage
These graphs don't exist until after the interview
questions.explain: Dense, detailed graphs are harder to read live and faster to misinterpret -- a prepared diagram walkthrough communicates more clearly in limited interview time.

questions.q: What is Driftwood's honest answer to "what would you do differently if ingestion needed to be closer to real-time?"
options: Move from scheduled batch COPY INTO to Snowpipe
Switch from Snowflake to a different data warehouse entirely
Remove Airflow orchestration entirely
There is no answer -- real-time ingestion is impossible in this architecture
questions.explain: This is the exact trade-off named back in Lesson 3 -- Snowpipe is the documented upgrade path if the freshness requirement ever genuinely changed.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say steps 4 and 5 (production practices and results) separate a strong candidate from most others?
options: Most candidates stop at a working pipeline (step 3) with no production practices around it -- steps 4-5 show you'd survive on a real data team
Steps 4 and 5 are optional and rarely discussed in real interviews
Steps 1-3 are unimportant and can be skipped entirely
Production practices are only relevant for AWS-based projects, not Snowflake ones
questions.explain: A pipeline that merely works is a tutorial; the production practices and measurable results are what demonstrate job-readiness.

questions.q: What specific change to Time Travel retention does this lesson name as the honest "at scale" answer for disaster recovery?
options: Increasing the current 1-day retention, understanding the storage-cost trade-off that comes with it
Removing Time Travel entirely to save costs
Switching all tables to transient to reduce retention costs
There is no planned change to Time Travel at scale
questions.explain: The lesson names a specific, honest scale answer: more people able to break production data justifies a longer self-service recovery window, at a real storage-cost trade-off.
